analysis.investment_thesis: Aditya Birla Sun Life AMC is a textbook asset-light compounder — 27% ROE, 64% operating margins, zero debt, and consistent 5/5 years of positive free cash flow, all riding the powerful secular story of India's rising mutual fund penetration (SIP culture going mainstream). The problem is price: at P/E 30x on ~15-20% recent earnings growth, the PEG sits around 1.5-2.0, which is the upper limit of what I'd pay.
key_strengths: Exceptional economics: 64.43% operating margin, 27% ROE, and D/E of 0.02 — essentially a toll booth on India's savings
Net profit CAGR of 19.6% over 8 years with 5/5 years OCF positive — rare consistency
Massive secular tailwind: India's mutual fund AUM-to-GDP ratio remains far below developed markets
key_risks: Recent earnings growth has decelerated: FY23 net profit INR 596 Cr → FY25 INR 931 Cr, implying ~12-15% 2-year CAGR vs the 8-year average of 19.6%
Promoter holds 74.82%, leaving limited float and potential overhang if stake is ever trimmed
Revenue growth at only 8.8% CAGR reflects fee compression pressure as competition from passive funds intensifies
red_flags: PEG ratio of ~1.5-2.0 exceeds my preferred threshold of <1.0 for a conviction buy
Revenue 8-year CAGR of 8.8% is modest — margin expansion has driven earnings, but that has limits
analysis.detailed_analysis:
ABSLAMC is the kind of business I love to own at the right price — an asset-light franchise collecting fees on an ever-growing pile of other people's money, with no meaningful debt, expanding margins, and a simple story any investor can understand. The India mutual fund penetration thesis is as visible as watching SIP ads on every cricket broadcast. Revenue grew from INR 1,235 Cr (FY20) to INR 1,982 Cr (FY25), and net profit from INR 494 Cr to INR 931 Cr — solid but not barn-burning.

At P/E 30x, I'd need to see earnings re-accelerate to 20%+ for this to be a screaming buy. Recent 2-year earnings CAGR is closer to 12-15%, putting the PEG at 1.5-2.0 — good business, fair-to-full price. I'd add aggressively on a 15-20% pullback.
